1	# Performance notes
2	
3	The nightly clash report runs over every booking of the next day across the whole estate: a handful of rooms (the big campuses have 2 to 4 bookable halls) with tens of thousands of bookings each, since halls are booked in 5-minute slots by many teams. Clashes are rare, a few hundred pairs on a bad night.
4	
5	`find_overlaps` therefore has to scale close to n log n in the number of bookings. Grouping by room does not help much because almost all bookings are in the same few rooms.
6

1	"""Clash detection between bookings."""
2	
3	from dataclasses import dataclass
4	
5	
6	@dataclass(frozen=True)
7	class Booking:
8	    id: str
9	    room: str
10	    start: int  # minutes since midnight
11	    end: int  # exclusive
12	
13	
14	def overlaps(a: Booking, b: Booking) -> bool:
15	    return a.room == b.room and a.start < b.end and b.start < a.end
16	
17	
18	def find_overlaps(bookings: list[Booking]) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
19	    """Return every clashing pair as (id_a, id_b) with id_a < id_b, sorted.
20	
21	    Two bookings clash when they are in the same room and their half-open
22	    intervals intersect. A booking fully inside a longer one clashes with it;
23	    a booking that ends exactly when another starts does not.
24	    """
25	    pairs: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
26	    for i in range(len(bookings)):
27	        a = bookings[i]
28	        for j in range(i + 1, len(bookings)):
29	            b = bookings[j]
30	            if overlaps(a, b):
31	                pairs.append((a.id, b.id) if a.id < b.id else (b.id, a.id))
32	    pairs.sort()
33	    return pairs

20	        b = Booking("b", "r1", 90, 150)

1	"""Plain-text clash report."""
2	
3	from .core import Booking, find_overlaps
4	
5	
6	def render(bookings: list[Booking]) -> str:
7	    by_id = {b.id: b for b in bookings}
8	    lines = []
9	    for a, b in find_overlaps(bookings):
10	        x, y = by_id[a], by_id[b]
11	        lines.append(f"{x.room}: {a} [{x.start}-{x.end}) clashes with {b} [{y.start}-{y.end})")
12	    return "\n".join(lines) + ("\n" if lines else "")

    """
    order = sorted(bookings, key=lambda b: b.start)
    # Per room, a heap of (end, index into order) for bookings not yet finished.
    running: dict[str, list[tuple[int, int]]] = {}
    pairs: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
    for i, b in enumerate(order):
        live = running.setdefault(b.room, [])
        while live and live[0][0] <= b.start:
            heapq.heappop(live)
        for _, j in live:
            a = order[j]
            # a.start <= b.start < a.end already holds; a zero- or
            # negative-length b still needs the other half of the test.
            if a.start < b.end:
                pairs.append((a.id, b.id) if a.id < b.id else (b.id, a.id))
        heapq.heappush(live, (b.end, i))
    pairs.sort()
    return pairs

import random, time
from overlaps.core import Booking, find_overlaps

def nightly(n, rooms=4, seed=3):
    """5-minute slots, mostly back-to-back, a few hundred real clashes."""
    r=random.Random(seed); out=[]; cursor={f"r{k}":0 for k in range(rooms)}
    for i in range(n):
        room=f"r{r.randrange(rooms)}"
        dur=5*r.randrange(1,13)
        start=cursor[room]
        if r.random()<0.01:            # rare double-book
            start=max(0,start-dur)
        cursor[room]=start+dur
        out.append(Booking(f"b{i:07d}",room,start,start+dur))
    r.shuffle(out)
    return out

prev=None
for n in (20_000,40_000,80_000,160_000,320_000):
    bs=nightly(n)
    t=time.perf_counter(); p=find_overlaps(bs); el=time.perf_counter()-t
    ratio=f"  x{el/prev:.2f}" if prev else ""
    print(f"n={n:>7}  {el:6.3f}s  {len(p):>6} clashes{ratio}")
    prev=el
